title_en: Diantou Longsheng Stone Factory v. Fuding Municipal People's Government — dispute over administrative measures for supporting superior and strong enterprises
keywords_en: Administrative; Administrative measures to support and strengthen the superior; Disputes over operational autonomy; First instance; Basic people's court; Fujian Province; Legal person; State organ; Administrative Procedure Law; Identification of specific administrative acts; Distinction between administrative guidance and specific administrative acts; Defendant's burden of proof; Confirmation of illegality; Administrative support and strengthening the superior; Basalt quarry supply; Operational autonomy
full_text_en:
Diantou Longsheng Stone Materials Factory v. People's Government of Fuding City — Dispute over Administrative Measures for Supporting the Excellent and Strengthening the Strong

Plaintiff: Diantou Longsheng Stone Materials Factory, Fuding City, Fujian Province. Address: Diantou Town, Fuding City.
Legal Representative: Su Jiasheng, Factory Director.
Agent ad litem: Cai Jingsai, Employee of Diantou Town Veterinary Station, Fuding City.

Defendant: People's Government of Fuding City, Fujian Province.
Legal Representative: Chen Mingsheng, Mayor of the City.
Agent ad litem: Zeng Feng, Lawyer from Fuding Minzhe Law Firm.

Third Party: Fujian Xuanwu Stone Materials Co., Ltd. Address: Fuding City CPPCC Building.
Legal Representative: Zhu Xiaotong, Chairman of the Board.

The plaintiff, Diantou Longsheng Stone Materials Factory of Fuding City, Fujian Province, dissatisfied with the "Opinions on Supporting the Excellent and Strengthening the Strong for Basalt Slabstone Processing Enterprises in 2001" issued by the defendant, the People's Government of Fuding City, Fujian Province, on March 13, 2001, in the form of Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document, filed a lawsuit with the Fuding City People's Court, Fujian Province.

The plaintiff alleged: The annual mining volume of basalt quarry stone in the mine is only 90,000 cubic meters, all of which is supplied by the third party, Fujian Xuanwu Stone Materials Co., Ltd., to over 920 stone processing enterprises in the city, with each processing enterprise receiving an average of less than 98 cubic meters. In 2000, the defendant, through Dingzhengban (2000) Nos. 59 and 60 Documents, set aside 8,000 cubic meters from the total volume of basalt quarry stone in the city to be supplied exclusively to 22 so-called supported enterprises. On March 13, 2001, the defendant issued Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document, stipulating that 31 enterprises would be supported through preferential increases in quarry stone supply. Calculated on this basis, 11,300 cubic meters of basalt quarry stone would need to be set aside this year to supply those so-called supported and strengthened enterprises. On average, each enterprise would have 12.28 cubic meters of quarry stone set aside. Moreover, among the 31 so-called supported and strengthened enterprises designated by the defendant, 26 had an output value of less than RMB 5 million, which did not meet the conditions set by the defendant itself for supporting the excellent and strengthening the strong. This practice of annually increasing the volume of set-aside quarry stone for support forced the plaintiff to reduce production year by year. The plaintiff argued that strong and advantageous enterprises can only emerge through fair competition and cannot be fostered through administrative means. Such practices by the defendant created inequality, undermined the social and economic order of fair competition, and fostered corruption through favoritism and backdoor dealings, constituting unlawful administration. The plaintiff requested the revocation of the defendant's Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document.

The defendant argued: The Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document was merely a non-mandatory administrative guidance document that did not directly produce legal consequences, issued only after obtaining consent from the administrative counterpart, the third party, Fujian Xuanwu Stone Materials Co., Ltd., regarding its business operations. For the plaintiff, this document neither established rights nor imposed obligations, and had no direct relationship with its interests. It did not constitute a specific administrative act as defined in Article 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and was not subject to administrative litigation. The plaintiff had no right to file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court regarding this document.

The defendant did not submit to the court the factual basis or legal basis for producing the Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document.

Prior to the hearing, the third party submitted a written application not to participate in the trial.

The Fuding City People's Court found after trial:

On March 13, 2001, the defendant, the People's Government of Fuding City, in order to promote the scaling-up and product upgrading of basalt stone enterprises in Fuding City, had its subordinate office issue Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document, approving the issuance of the "Opinions of the Office of the Fuding Municipal Industrial Leading Group on Supporting the Excellent and Strengthening the Strong for Basalt Slabstone Processing Enterprises in 2001." This document designated 31 slabstone enterprises with a certain production scale to be supported in 2001. The document stipulated that the third party, Fujian Xuanwu Stone Materials Co., Ltd., should increase the annual supply of basalt quarry stone by 500 cubic meters for each of the 10 enterprises with annual sales revenue of over RMB 10 million, and by 300 cubic meters for each of the 21 enterprises with annual sales revenue of over RMB 5 million. The document was issued in the form of a notice to various townships (towns) People's Governments, subdistrict offices, relevant municipal units, and the Long'an Development Zone Management Committee in Fuding City. During the trial of this case, the People's Government of Fuding City issued Dingzhengban (2001) No. 74 Document on July 13, 2001, deciding to cease the implementation of Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document.

The Fuding City People's Court held:

The raw materials used in the production of basalt stone enterprises in Fuding City are all supplied by the third party, Fujian Xuanwu Stone Materials Co., Ltd., and the supply volume is limited. Under these circumstances, the defendant, the People's Government of Fuding City, approved and issued the "Opinions of the Office of the Municipal Industrial Leading Group on Supporting the Excellent and Strengthening the Strong for Basalt Slabstone Processing Enterprises in 2001" through Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document. Although this document did not establish rights or obligations for the plaintiff, Diantou Longsheng Stone Materials Factory, by forcibly intervening in the sales method of Fujian Xuanwu Stone Materials Co., Ltd., it directly affected the operational rights of Diantou Longsheng Stone Materials Factory. Therefore, for Diantou Longsheng Stone Materials Factory, this document fell within the circumstance of "considering that an administrative authority has infringed upon its lawful right to autonomous operation" as stipulated in Article 11, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Administrative Procedure Law, and constituted a specific administrative act as defined in Article 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law, which falls within the scope of administrative litigation accepted by the People's Court. Diantou Longsheng Stone Materials Factory had the right to file an administrative lawsuit. The People's Court's acceptance of this case complies with the provisions of Article 1, Paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which states: "If a citizen, legal person, or other organization, dissatisfied with an administrative act of an organ or organization with state administrative authority or its staff, initiates a lawsuit in accordance with the law, it shall fall within the scope of administrative litigation accepted by the People's Court." The defendant, the People's Government of Fuding City, argued that the Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document was an administrative guidance document with no mandatory effect, not a specific administrative act, and therefore not subject to administrative litigation. This argument was untenable.

Article 32 of the Administrative Procedure Law provides: "The defendant bears the burden of proof for the specific administrative act it has undertaken and shall provide evidence and the regulatory documents on which the act is based." Article 43 provides that the defendant shall, within 10 days of receiving a copy of the statement of complaint, submit to the People's Court the relevant materials concerning the specific administrative act and file a statement of defense. Article 26, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The defendant shall, within 10 days of receiving a copy of the statement of complaint, submit a statement of defense and provide the evidence and basis for the specific administrative act at the time it was undertaken; if the defendant fails to provide or fails to provide within the time limit without justifiable reasons, the specific administrative act shall be deemed to have no evidence or basis." In this case, after receiving a copy of the statement of complaint, the defendant, the People's Government of Fuding City, within the statutory time limit, only filed a statement of defense and did not provide the factual basis or legal basis for making Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document, and could not prove that the document was lawful, so it should be revoked in accordance with the law. During the trial of this case, the People's Government of Fuding City had already ceased implementing Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document, so continuing to render a judgment revoking the document would be of no practical significance.

Accordingly, the Fuding City People's Court, in accordance with Article 50, Paragraph 3 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "If the defendant changes the original specific administrative act and the plaintiff does not withdraw the lawsuit, and the People's Court, upon examination, finds that the original specific administrative act is unlawful, it shall render a judgment confirming its illegality," rendered the following judgment on July 19, 2001:

It is confirmed that the Dingzhengban (2001) No. 14 Document, issued on March 13, 2001, by the defendant, the People's Government of Fuding City, Fujian Province, is illegal.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, neither party appealed, and the judgment has become legally effective.
